subject: Order Form redlines: IP demarcation and feedback license — proposal and evidence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@brightline.com>, Brightline Legal <legal@brightline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines: IP demarcation and feedback license — initial redlines and evidence request

Hi Priya / Brightline legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion I've attached a focused set of redlines to the Order Form + Exhibit A that narrow the open points to three items: (1) output ownership of customer-provided content, (2) training/data use (opt-in vs. opt-out), and (3) the scope of any feedback or telemetry license.

Short summary of our position:
- Customer retains exclusive ownership of outputs that are generated solely from customer-provided prompts and data.
- Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry to operate and improve the service, but we will not train public or base models on identifiable customer content without explicit opt-in.
- We propose a limited, non-exclusive feedback license that permits operational use and product improvement only, with a prohibition on resale or redistribution of customer outputs.

Action items we need from Brightline legal to move forward:
1) Confirm whether Brightline will accept a narrow feedback license limited to service improvement (we included sample language in the attached redlines).
2) If you require stronger language on training restrictions, please specify the exact carveouts (e.g., allowed internal evals, anonymized model tuning on aggregated signals, etc.).
3) Provide any procurement evidence checklist items needed on our side (encryption/KMS screenshots, SOC2 evidence pointers).

Attachments: proposed_orderform_redlines_v3.docx (only the changed clauses), evidence_kms_config.pdf (redacted screenshots of KMS + key rotation schedule), feedback-license-draft.txt (plain text of the proposed license).

Timeline: we can accept a counter-redline by EOD Friday 7 May and aim to finalize for signature next week. If you prefer, we can do a 20-min legal-to-legal call tomorrow.

Thanks — kim

--

From: Brightline Legal <legal@brightline.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines: IP demarcation and feedback license — initial redlines and evidence request

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Narrow questions from our side after a quick read:
1) "Customer retains exclusive ownership of outputs" — please confirm whether that includes derivatives produced by our integration (e.g., when Brightline combines outputs with third-party data). We generally want downstream rights protections.
2) On training: the language is close to what we need, but our security team requires an explicit statement that no customer content will be used to train any models other customers have access to (including aggregated improvements) unless we opt in via an explicit checkbox per Order Form.
3) Regarding the feedback license, we prefer a temporal limitation for evaluation use (e.g., 12 months) if Redwood will want to use non-identifiable outputs for product improvement.

If you can send a redline that addresses (a) downstream derivative clarity, (b) absolute non-training guarantee without opt-in, and (c) time-bound feedback license we can move faster. Also send any SOC2 artifact IDs or PRD references your security team wants to surface to our SOC team (we will run a short evidence intake).

Thanks —
Brightline Legal (on behalf of Priya & Marcus)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: suggested compromise language for Brightline redlines

Kim / Laura — quick internal note following Priya's reply. I drafted some compromise language that should be acceptable to procurement and keep product options open. Key points in draft:
- Define "Customer Outputs" narrowly as outputs generated from Customer Content + Customer Prompts; carve out cases where Customer merges outputs with third-party data (downstream use) — allow Customer to seek downstream rights, but Redwood keeps a Product Improvement license to aggregated de-identified signals only.
- Training: provide a contractual guarantee that we will not incorporate identifiable Customer Content into any model used by third parties; allow Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified signals for continuous improvement, subject to Brightline opt-out via a per-Order Form checkbox.
- Feedback license: change to a perpetual, non-exclusive license for internal product improvement only, with an option for a time-bound evaluation-only clause if Brightline insists; include prohibition on resale.

I'll paste the exact suggested clause in the next message so we can copy into the doc. If you'd rather legal handle direct redline exchange, I'm happy to join the call with Brightline legal tomorrow.

—Ben
Senior Counsel, Commercial

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines: IP demarcation and feedback license — updated compromise redline attached

Priya / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've updated the redlines to reflect the compromise Ben suggested and added an explicit checkbox option on the Order Form for training opt-in/opt-out. Highlights of the attached v3:
- Customer Outputs: expressly defined as "Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and Customer Prompts". We added language giving Customer the right to combine Outputs with other data and to assert ownership over the resulting derived product, subject to mutually agreed commercial terms.
- Training protections: Redwood agrees not to use identifiable Customer Content to train models accessible to third parties. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for internal product improvement unless the Customer opts out on the Order Form checkbox.
- Feedback license: now reads as a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated, non-identifiable feedback for product improvement only; prohibited uses include resale, standalone redistribution, or training of public models absent opt-in.

I've attached: proposed_orderform_redlines_v3.docx (changes tracked), evidence_kms_config.pdf (redacted screenshots + key rotation schedule), and feedback-license-draft.txt. Also included is a DocuSign link if you want to accept these changes and move to signature: https://docusign.com/link/ABCDEF-12345

Next steps: if Brightline can confirm the opt-out checkbox language and whether the downstream-derivative carveout works, we can finalize this week. If you prefer a short legal-to-legal call I can set up 20 minutes today.

Best,
Kim

Kim —

Thanks for the revised redline and the artifacts. Procurement and legal are aligned in principle and appreciate the checkbox approach for training opt-in/opt-out. Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Replace the open-ended "internal product improvement" phrase with a short definition (we suggest: "internal product improvement means: performance tuning, bug fixes, and service reliability improvements not resulting in redistribution of Customer Outputs").
2) For the feedback license, we'd like a 12-month evaluation window on use of aggregated outputs for product improvement, after which Redwood must either (a) obtain explicit opt-in for continued use or (b) purge the associated de-identified dataset used for that customer.

If Redwood accepts those two adjustments we can route for signature. I attached a one-page counter-markup that shows the two line changes.

Priya
VP, Legal Ops
Brightline Systems
